nicheLogic:
━━ ARTIST CONTEXT ━━
Thierno (aka Braz) — R&B, Afrobeats, Hip-Hop. From Portsmouth, Northampton and London. Self-managed. Two singles out (Flaws, Can't Imagine via DistroKid). Single 3 incoming. Vocal authenticity is his unfair advantage — raw unproduced vocals consistently outperform polished content. The tension between small-city origin and big-city ambition is his story angle no competitor can copy.

━━ AUDIENCE SEGMENTS ━━
- PRIMARY (16-24, UK R&B/Afrobeats fans): Follow artists who feel real before they blow up. Share clips when the music matches their exact current mood. They need to feel like they discovered him. Trigger: social currency of being first.
- SECONDARY (Music discovery audience): Find artists on TikTok before Spotify algorithmic push. They share to signal taste. Trigger: 'I heard this before it was everywhere.'
- TERTIARY (Black British music community): Pride in authentic UK artists doing it without industry backing. Share to amplify 'one of ours.' Trigger: cultural ownership + underdog narrative.

━━ CONTENT PILLARS (ranked by virality ceiling) ━━
1. RAW VOCAL MOMENT — unpolished bedroom or studio clip, phone quality fine, zero production needed. The rawness IS the hook. If the vocal is good, the algorithm rewards it. Ceiling: 500K+
2. BEHIND THE SCENES — studio sessions, late nights making music, the struggle between day-to-day life and the music grind. People follow the journey before they follow the artist. Ceiling: 200K+
3. SNIPPET DROP — 15-30s of an unreleased track. Never the full song. Leave them wanting. The comment section becomes a pre-save campaign. Ceiling: 200K+ with stream spike on release day.
4. REACTION / PERSONAL STORY — a real moment from his life with the right track underneath. Relatable caption. No script. Ceiling: 150K+
5. RELEASE PUSH — direct stream CTA, lyric graphic, cover art reveal. Lower viral ceiling but converts existing fans to streams. Ceiling: 50K. Never lead with this.

━━ SCROLL-STOP HOOKS FOR MUSIC CONTENT ━━
The music niche has one rule: the audio IS the hook. If the first 0.5 seconds of audio doesn't stop the scroll, nothing else will.
- FALSETTO OR HIGH NOTE FIRST — the brain registers unexpected pitch change as a pattern interrupt. Drop straight into the most impressive vocal moment.
- RAW + IMPERFECT — one-take bedroom vocals with audible room noise outperform studio quality 3:1. Imperfection signals authenticity.
- LYRIC IDENTITY TRIGGER — open with a lyric that makes the listener think 'that's exactly how I feel.' Comment section writes itself.
- CONTRAST HOOK — 'they said I'd never make it' over a clip of him singing something undeniably good. Narrative + music = share trigger.
- NEVER: start with talking, announcing the song name, showing the cover art, or a countdown. Open on the music.

━━ PLATFORM-SPECIFIC INTELLIGENCE ━━
TIKTOK: Sounds strategy is everything. If a track gets used as a sound by other creators, streams compound. Post raw vocal clips at 9-11pm. Use trending audio under BTS content but original audio for vocal clips. Duets and stitches from fans = biggest organic multiplier.
INSTAGRAM: Reels favour saves. Post lyric graphics and snippet drops for saves. Stories for personal/behind-scenes. Collab posts with other UK artists = reach multiplier.
SPOTIFY: TikTok → Spotify pipeline is the play. Every viral TikTok clip should link to Spotify. 'Can't Imagine' is discovery-driven — lean into that with more discovery-style content (raw, relatable, emotional).
YOUTUBE: Long-form studio vlogs, full song performances. Lower priority but builds the archive.

━━ SEASONAL INTELLIGENCE ━━
- Summer (May-Aug): Feel-good bangers, upbeat Afrobeats energy, outdoor vibes. Post 6-9pm. High energy first frame.
- Autumn/Winter (Sep-Feb): Late-night moody R&B, emotional tracks, atmospheric aesthetics. Post 8-11pm. Low light, intimate setting.
- Always match music mood to season — posting a summer banger in November kills the algorithm momentum.

━━ THE UNFAIR ADVANTAGE ━━
Chris Brown, Tory Lanez, Justin Bieber have production budgets. Thierno has something they can't buy back — the raw pre-fame energy. Every piece of content should feel like you're watching someone before the world knew them. That authenticity is the entire brand. The moment it gets too polished, it loses the thing that makes it work.

━━ SHARE TRIGGERS ━━
- Discovery fans share because: 'I found him before he blew up' → social currency
- Mood-matchers share because: 'this song is exactly how I feel right now' → emotional validation
- UK Black community shares because: 'one of ours, doing it properly' → cultural pride
- Music heads share because: 'the vocal ability is undeniable' → taste signalling

━━ WHAT COMPETITORS AREN'T DOING ━━
Chris Brown / Tory Lanez / Justin Bieber content is all high-production, distant, celebrity-coded. The gap is: authentic, close, pre-fame energy from someone who sounds as good but feels real and accessible. Own the 'before the deal' space.
